narrative_markdown:
## Today's Forecast

Clearer than yesterday; temperatures and winds little changed. Dry, with thunder possible from the morning, peaking this evening. 31°C / 87°F high, 19°C / 66°F low. Sky partly cloudy early as reported, mostly cloudy at midday and mostly cloudy in the evening. Wind SW at midday; gusts to 37 km/h (20 kt). UV index 9.5 (very high). Air quality 52 (moderate) at Ochieng' Avenue, Kisumu Central, the highest of 3 stations. As of 06:01, reports through 03:00: no rain; no thunder; high so far 22°C / 72°F; low so far 21°C / 70°F; peak sustained 6 km/h; sky partly cloudy.

## Extended Outlook

NEXT THREE DAYS see temperatures and winds much the same through Friday, with showers and thunderstorms likely each day. Wednesday will be partly cloudy with a high range of 30–33 °C, rain from all four models (0.8–6.1 mm) and thunder likely. Thursday stays mostly cloudy, high 30–32 °C, rain 1.4–4.9 mm, thunder likely. Friday remains mostly cloudy, high 27–30 °C, rain 0.4–15.2 mm, thunder likely. The Day+3 call gives a high of 27 °C and low of 20 °C, while the Day+7 call projects a high of 27–30 °C and low of 19 °C. RECORD notes ECMWF as the best rain record holder for both Day+3 and Day+7.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential

Peak CAPE values exceed the thunderstorm threshold, with Best Match at 2580 J/kg and ECMWF at 2080 J/kg, indicating a risk of strong up‑drafts. Thunder possible from the morning, peaking this evening, could bring sudden gusts well above the forecast 37 km/h (20 kt) ashore. No explicit met service warning was issued.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters

Peak gust 26 km/h (14 kt). Any thunderstorm brings sudden gusts well above this figure; the water is unsafe while one is nearby.

## Detailed Discussion

### Synoptic Overview

Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the northwest (1010 hPa) and highest toward the southeast (1016 hPa) — a 6 hPa spread, a moderate large-scale gradient. Pressure is also falling toward the east, north, southwest — a large-scale feature building in that direction, though this sampling cannot say how fast or whether it will reach here. Pressure overhead is falling. Sampling is a nine-point ring at 12-degree spacing, so this locates a direction, not a centre or a front. Across the basin's 5 points, pressure today sits between 1013.5 and 1015.5 hPa, falling by 2.4 hPa over three days. Pressure here over the last 24 hours: -1.6 hPa.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes

REVIEW finds no model clearly superior at Day+0, though Best Match slightly under‑forecasts peak wind and ECMWF slightly over‑forecasts overnight lows while under‑forecasting daytime highs and peak wind. GFS systematically over‑forecasts daytime highs and under‑forecasts peak wind. The call's high of 31 °C aligns with ECMWF's slight under‑forecast and GFS's slight over‑forecast. ECMWF holds the best rain record for Day+7, while GFS is the weakest. KMD provided no forecast, limiting direct comparison. DATA SUFFICIENCY notes 47 checks at Day+0, giving a settled picture despite uneven KMD coverage.
